proposition.claim:
Equation reference: eq:claimed. Theorem 1.16, printed p. 211/PDF 23, asserts, for an open \(U\subset\Omega\) and \(\delta>0\), \[
 \nu_\star(V_\delta)=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \nu_\star(\overline U)=0 ,
 \qquad
 U_\delta=\{x\in\Omega:\operatorname{dist}(x,U)\le\delta\},\
 V_\delta=U_\delta\setminus U .\] The overline on \(U\) in the conclusion was confirmed in the page image; text extraction suppresses it. The preceding prose allows general regular subdomains and does not require \(\overline U\subset\Omega\) or a positive distance to the exterior boundary.

Section 7.3, printed p. 273/PDF 85, invokes Proposition 4.15. The latter, printed p. 252/PDF 64, writes \(U_\delta\subset\Omega\), but this is already automatic for the clipped definition (1.67). Its proof uses Proposition 3.11, printed p. 242/PDF 54, where a smooth cutoff equals one on \(U_{\delta/2}\) and vanishes outside \(U_\delta\), and the test field \(X(z)=z\chi_\delta(z)\) is inserted in the compact-support identity (3.19). Such a cutoff is unavailable when \(U_{\delta/2}\) reaches \(\partial\Omega\). This is a boundary-support obstruction, not a numerical approximation error.
